problem: Language-described navigation goals carry rich semantics but lack precise geometry, and RGB-D-based semantic mapping suffers from noisy depth in real environments, which hurts grounding and navigation.
motivation: Real-world robots need to turn language goals into accurate geometric targets for motion planning. RGB-D gives rich semantics but noisy depth, while LiDAR gives precise geometry, so fusing the two could reduce grounding noise.
key_idea: Build a unified semantic map by cross-modally aligning LiDAR point clouds with RGB-D semantic data, so language goals are grounded into precise geometric representations for navigation.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablations could be read. The abstract claims that LiDAR's precise depth compensates for noisy RGB-D depth when grounding semantics, and that this improves navigation over RGB-D-only methods.
method: Environment reconstruction: reconstructs the physical environment into a map for navigation.
Language goal grounding: grounds language-based goals into detailed geometric representations usable by the planner.
Cross-modal alignment: fuses LiDAR point clouds (precise depth) with RGB-D (rich semantics, noisy depth) to reduce grounding noise.
Unified map: integrates semantic, geometric and contextual relationships in a single map.
